mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO falls for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% in the same month signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2.5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand and construction activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where both PAYEMS and HOUST rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and prompts preemptive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE is below 3.5% for three straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for five consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit forecasts, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where RSAFS declines for five consecutive months.
